title: runtime-benchmarking-harness-perf-regression-notes
content:
Executive summary

This document captures the current design and notes for the serving runtime benchmarking harness and perf-regression workflow. It focuses on three areas of microbench coverage: kernel-level microbenchmarks (matmul, attention, quantized kernels), scheduling/batching behavior, and KV cache performance (prefix reuse, cache hit/miss latency). It also documents tracing conventions, sample traces, and proposed regression detection/alerting thresholds for CI and nightly jobs.

Goals
- Provide reproducible microbenchmarks that isolate kernel and scheduler behavior.
- Capture realistic end-to-end traces for representative request mixes.
- Detect regressions early via CI (quick checks) and nightly stability runs (full suite).
- Produce actionable trace output that points to root causes (kernel slowdown, lock contention, memory stalls, serialization).

Scope and constraints
- Focus on inference runtime components used in hosted & dedicated modes. Private deployments will reuse the harness but may need env-specific configs.
- Target hardware: A100 40GB, A10G, and one 4xV100-like emulation node for legacy comparison.
- Benchmarks must be deterministic when possible: fixed RNG seeds, controlled thermal states where applicable.
- Avoid cloud provider-managed autoscaling during microbench runs.

Harness architecture (high level)
- microbench-runner: Go binary for microbench orchestration, collects metrics via Prometheus client, emits JSON artifacts.
- trace-probe: lightweight instrumentation layer that emits OTLP traces to local collector.
- bench-store: S3-compatible storage bucket for artifacts (metrics.json, traces/*.json, kernel-profiles/*.prof).
- ci-integration: GitHub Actions job that runs a subset of microbenches for PRs; nightly runs on dedicated infra capture full suite.

Microbench types and configs
1) Kernel microbenches- Purpose: measure raw compute kernels in isolation (GEMM, fused-attn, rotary/flash-attn variants, quantized-matmul).- Configs: batch_size in {1,4,16,64}, seq_len in {16,128,512,1024}, dtype in {fp16, bf16, int8}, kv_cache:false- Output: per-op latency distribution (p50/p90/p99), flop rate (TFLOPS), GPU SM utilization, memory bandwidth utilization (GB/s), kernel occupancy.- Example command: bin/microbench --kernel fused_attn --seq_len 1024 --batch 8 --dtype fp16 --profile kernel-profiles/attn-1024-b8.fp

2) Scheduling / batching microbenches- Purpose: exercise the request scheduler, batching heuristics, and queueing under varying QPS and request size distributions.- Workloads: synthetic uniform short prompts (avg tokens 64), mixed chat (avg tokens 256, with occasional 1024 long), high-concurrency short requests.- Metrics: end-to-end latency (service p50/p95/p99), batching latency distribution (time spent waiting in queue), batch sizes achieved, dropped requests, request fairness metrics.- Key knobs: max_batch_ms, batch_size_limit, scheduler_policy={latency_first, throughput_first, hybrid}.- Example command: bin/scheduler-bench --policy hybrid --arrival-dist poisson --qps 600 --seq-dist mixed --duration 10m --out artifacts/scheduler-hybrid-600.json

3) KV cache microbenches- Purpose: measure prefix reuse and KV-cache lookup/eviction performance.- Configs: prefix_reuse in {0%, 50%, 90%}, kv_store in {in-memory, GPU-sharded, host-sharded}, eviction_policy in {LRU, clock}- Metrics: hit_rate, avg_lookup_latency, miss_penalty (time to refill), memory footprint, memcpy bandwidth, KV cache lock contention (mutex contention time).- Scenarios: streaming chat where prefix is reused heavily; API burst where no reuse; multi-tenant mix.- Example command: bin/kvbench --prefix_reuse 0.9 --vec_store gpu --seq_len 512 --clients 64 --duration 15m --out artifacts/kv-90pct.json

Instrumentation and trace conventions
- Tracing must correlate to a single request via trace_id and include spans for: request_incoming -> scheduling -> batch_assembly -> kernel_exec (one or more) -> kv_lookup -> token_emit -> response_write.
- Each span should have attributes: span.kind, model_version, device_id, batch_size, seq_len, dtype, kernel_name (if kernel_exec), kv_hit boolean (if kv_lookup).- Use OTLP/exporter that can emit both Jaeger-friendly JSON and raw OTLP protobufs. Traces are stored under traces/<date>/<run-id>/trace.json.

Sample trace (abridged)
Span: request_incoming (start=0.000ms, dur=0.10ms)
Span: scheduling (start=0.10ms, dur=12.5ms) attributes: {queue_pos:3, waited_ms:12.4} 
Span: batch_assembly (start=12.6ms, dur=1.2ms) attributes: {batch_size:8} 
Span: kv_lookup (start=13.8ms, dur=0.8ms) attributes: {kv_hit:true, hit_rate_bucket:0.9} 
Span: kernel_exec:fused_attn (start=14.6ms, dur=5.2ms) attributes: {kernel_variant:flash_attn_v2, sm_util:82.1, mem_bw:420GB/s} 
Span: token_emit (start=19.8ms, dur=0.6ms)

Notes on trace interpretation
- If kernel_exec spans show increased dur but SM util remains high and mem_bw unchanged, suspect kernel algorithm regression (e.g., extra copies, poor tiling).
- If kernel_exec dur increases while SM util drops, may indicate increased CPU-side stalls or PCIe transfers (check memcpy spans).
- Large scheduling wait times correlating with small batch sizes implies scheduler heuristic mismatch; increase max_batch_ms or change policy.

Regression detection rules (proposed)
- Quick CI checks (PR-level): run ~10 fast microbenches (kernel-only, small seq lengths). Fail PR if: median kernel p50 increases > 15% relative to baseline snapshot for the same commit family.
- Nightly stability: full suite. Trigger alerts if:
  - median end-to-end latency increases > 5% and p95 increases > 10% across majority (>60%) of representative workloads.
  - any kernel p99 increases by > 20% or its TFLOPS drops > 10%.
  - KV cache hit latency avg increases > 15% or hit_rate drops > 5 percentage points.
- Always require manual triage for flaky signals; regression signal must be reproducible in a second run in the same env.

Baseline snapshots and storage
- Baseline artifacts are stored under bench-store/baselines/<commit-hash>/metrics.json and kernel-profiles/. Use commit tagging in bench metadata to link baselines to code state.
- For every run store: metrics.json, traces/*.json, stdout.log, kernel-profiles/*.prof, environment.txt (nvidia-smi, rocm-smi where applicable), gitmeta.txt.

CI integration and gating
- PR job: .github/workflows/microbench-pr.yml runs a lightweight set (10–15 mins). Artifacts uploaded to PR. Automated check compares against baseline stored in bench-store/pr-baseline/latest.json.
- Nightly: scheduled runner with dedicated reserved GPU pool, runs full suite (4–6 hours). Notifications posted to #eng-serving-runtime and to an on-call rotation if thresholds hit.
- Triage workflow: when alert fires, triage ticket auto-created in Jira (RINF-REG-<timestamp>) with links to artifacts. Owner on-call SRE + responsible code owners.

Example microbench results (representative)
- fused_attn, seq_len=1024, batch=8, dtype=fp16: p50=4.9ms, p90=6.8ms, p99=9.4ms, TFLOPS=110, sm_util=83%
- matmul_q8, M=4096,N=4096,K=4096, batch=1: p50=3.1ms, p90=4.9ms, p99=7.1ms, approx 62 TFLOPS (quantized path)
- KV bench, 90% prefix reuse, gpu-sharded: hit_rate=0.904, avg_lookup=0.65ms, miss_penalty=7.1ms
- Scheduler hybrid, qps=600, mixed seq: e2e p50=18.2ms, p95=42.7ms, p99=128.4ms, avg batch_size=6.7

Recent perf regression notes (observed)
- 2026-01-28: nightly run showed fused_attn p99 increase ~28% vs baseline. Trace showed kernel_exec increased dur while sm_util unchanged. Kernel profile revealed an extra memcpy call introduced by PR #421 (linked). Reverted memcpy change in PR #430 reduced p99 back to baseline.
- 2026-02-05: scheduler p95 regression for short prompts during high QPS. Traces showed increased batch assembly waits; root cause was a change to the default max_batch_ms (lowered from 12ms to 8ms) in config PR #415. Reverted to 12ms and added heuristic to avoid starvation of short requests.
- 2026-02-12: KV cache lookup latency spike under multi-tenant test. Investigation found lock contention on host-sharded store due to a pathological eviction pattern (large prefix churn). Mitigation: introduce per-shard locks and adaptive eviction watermarking (PR #447).

Open action items
- [Owner: Jamal] Add kernel-level microbench for rotary/ALiBi variants and include perf counters (L2 hit rate, dram read/write) by 2026-02-28.
- [Owner: Priya] Implement automated comparison runner that replays failed benchmarks twice before creating a triage ticket. ETA 2026-03-08.
- [Owner: Maya] Add docs for trace span naming conventions and attribute schema, then land in repo. TODO: unify with observability team.
- Add a synthetic workload generator that can mimic customer prompt distributions; tie to per-customer daily runs for high-value customers.

Test data and reproducibility notes
- Use fixed RNG seeds in microbench runner. Document hardware thermal state and GPU persistence settings in environment.txt.
- For nightly runs capture GPU power cap and clock settings. Where possible, lock clocks to stable values to reduce noise.

Appendix: example commands and artifacts
- Run all kernel microbenches on a single device:
  bin/microbench --all-kernels --device 0 --out artifacts/allkernels-$(date +%F).json
- Run scheduler stress test (poisson arrivals):
  bin/scheduler-bench --policy latency_first --arrival-dist poisson --qps 900 --duration 20m --out artifacts/scheduler-latency-900.json
- Collect traces locally and upload to bench-store:
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 bin/microbench --kernel fused_attn --trace --out traces/run-2026-02-17.json && aws s3 cp traces/run-2026-02-17.json s3://bench-store/traces/2026-02-17/
